newsitem.title: USA: 97/98 Brazilian coffee seen at 24 mln bags-attache.
newsitem.headline: 97/98 Brazilian coffee seen at 24 mln bags-attache.

text.p: Brazilian coffee output in marketing year 1997/98 (July/June) is forecast at 24 million bags because coffee trees will be in an off year of the production cycle, a U.S. agricultural attache said in a report made public on Tuesday.
The report, prepared by an attache with the U.S. embassy in Sao Paulo, said arabica production was forecast at 19.4 million bags and robusta production at 4.6 million bags, the report said.
"Coffee trees are predominantly in the off-year of the biannual production cycle, resulting in the expected lower production," the report said.

"The quality of the beans for MY 1997/98 is likely to be lower than that of the previous season, due to the excessive number of flowerings that occurred in some coffee producing areas, such as in parts of the states of Minas Gerais, Sao Paulo and Parana," the report said.
The attache report also said that Brazilian coffee production was revised for marketing year 1996-97 (July/June) to 27.5 million bags, up 6.5 percent from the previous estimate.

Last month, the U.S. Agriculture Department estimated Brazil's 1996/97 crop at 27.5 million bags and its 1997/98 crop at at 28.0 million bags. Although the estimate was questioned by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries, the agency said it stood by its production estimates.
The Brazilian government previously estimated coffee production of 25-26 million bags for 1996-97 and 22 million for 1997-98.
The agricultural attache report was dated May 12, although it was not released to the public until Tuesday.

The report also said that Brazilian domestic coffee consumption for marketing year 1996/97 remained unchanged at 11 million bags. Domestic consumption in marketing year 1997/98 was forecast at 12 million bags.

"The increase in the domestic consumption is mostly due to the stable economy which came about through the implementation of the Brazilian Government's economic plan in July 1994, which increased the purchasing power of low income groups," the report said.

Brazilian coffee exports were revised upward to 18.2 million bags for marketing year 1996/97, or 10 percent higher than previously expected, the report said. Coffee exports for marketing year 1997/98 were forecast at 17.5 million bags, including green coffee exports at 15 million bags and soluble coffee exports at 2.5 million bags.
The attache report said U.S. estimates of ending stocks for marketing year 1996/97 remained unchanged at 14.3 million bags. The current Brazilian Government stock level is 12.6 million bags.
